title: Manpower Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC M&RA
raw_text:
1.     MOS 0102, Manpower Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC M&RA

    a. Summary. Manpower Officers plan, coordinate, execute and/or
supervise the functions of administration (general administration,
operational administration, manpower administration, and personnel
administration) in their respective commands and organizations. Manpower
Officers coordinate with MOS 0170 Personnel Officers for matters of personnel
administration, for which the installation personnel administration center
(IPAC) has primary cognizance. Manpower Officers serve as advisors to
commanders for administrative matters. Manpower Officers are MAGTF officers,
who support operations with policies and programs affecting service members
in areas other than training and logistics. Duties at the company grade
level receiving and routing correspondence, maintaining command files and
directives, overseeing forms management programs, personnel strength
reporting, processing awards and decorations, providing expertise on
performance evaluations, safeguarding classified material, overseeing unit-
level legal matters, casualty reporting and supervising unit-level postal
functions. Duties at the field grade level include overseeing the four
functional areas of administration, S-1 section, personnel administration
section, civilian manpower section, G1 operations section, manpower plans and
policy development, and military and civilian manpower planning and staffing.
Billets include Unit S-1 officer, manpower officer, G-1 operations officer,
G-1 adjutant, deputy G-1, and the assistant chief of staff (AC/S G-1) in the
operating forces, supporting establishment, and joint assignments.

       b.    Prerequisites.    None.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Basic Manpower Officer Course (M03AAF8)
conducted at Personnel Administration School, MCB Camp Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (d), Personnel and Administration Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Administrative Services Managers 11-3011.

       f.    Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
